items.review_rationale: Read universal quantification over all elements of the extension field with the nonzero polynomial relation over the base field; the existence of one algebraic element is not enough to make the whole extension algebraic.

references.phrase: algebraic element of E over F

references.context: Univariate polynomial over the embedded base field whose coefficients are not all zero

references.phrase: every element of E satisfies some polynomial
references.disposition: The defining universal quantifier is essential; this is stronger than asserting the existence of a single algebraic element.

items.review_rationale: Read finite ring-map presentation through a polynomial R-algebra quotient with finite generators and finite relations; distinguished ring algebra presentation from finite presentation of an R-module.

references.context: Commutative polynomial R-algebra on finitely many formal variables x_i
Ideal generated by a finite list of polynomial relations in R[x_1,…,x_n]
Ring obtained by factoring the polynomial algebra by the relation ideal

references.phrase: R-algebra isomorphism from the quotient to S
references.context: Ring isomorphism commuting with the given structure maps from R, not merely an R-module isomorphism

references.disposition: Both generators and defining equations must be finite; a finitely generated R-algebra need not be finitely presented over an arbitrary R.

items.review_rationale: Read finite type as generation of S by finitely many elements as an R-algebra, equivalently a quotient of a finite-variable polynomial ring; did not smuggle in finite generation of the kernel ideal.

references.phrase: R-algebra generated by finitely many elements
references.context: Smallest unital R-subalgebra of S containing a finite list of elements equals S
Finite-variable polynomial ring over R with the universal assignment to algebra generators
Presentation as a quotient with no finite-generation assumption on the ideal of polynomial relations

references.disposition: Finite type constrains the generators; finite presentation would additionally constrain relations and is not inferred.

items.review_rationale: Read the Cohen–Macaulay condition for a Noetherian local ring, identifying its unique maximal ideal, local-module depth of R itself and Krull dimension of R, not the dimension of an arbitrary finitely generated module.

references.phrase: depth_m(R) of R as a local module

references.disposition: This is the Cohen–Macaulay criterion for the ring itself; equality with the dimension of a different module is not asserted.
